subsystems.name: Chassis
subsystems.role: a folded nanostructure roughly 10–100 nm across that holds every other part in a fixed geometry.
parts: alternative protein cages or DNA bricks

subsystems.name: Sensing and logic
subsystems.role: recognises molecular markers and decides whether to act.

subsystems.name: Actuators
subsystems.role: moves a part of the robot or opens a payload.

subsystems.name: Payload and release
subsystems.role: carries a drug, enzyme or gene-editing complex and exposes it only at the target.

subsystems.name: Stealth shell
subsystems.role: keeps the structure intact in blood and hidden from immune clearance.

subsystems.name: External control
subsystems.role: lets an operator outside the body see, steer or switch the robot.

buildSteps.title: Design in software
buildSteps.detail: A target shape is broken into a scaffold path plus staple sequences, then folding and unwanted base-pairing are checked computationally.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the strands
buildSteps.detail: The long scaffold is grown in bacteria from a viral genome and purified; hundreds of short staple strands are made by chemical oligonucleotide synthesis.

buildSteps.title: Fold the structure
buildSteps.detail: Scaffold and staples are mixed in a magnesium-rich buffer, heated and slowly cooled so each staple pulls its two matching regions together — a process that takes hours.

buildSteps.title: Verify the shape
buildSteps.detail: Atomic force microscopy or cryo-electron microscopy confirms the folded object matches the design, one molecule at a time.

buildSteps.title: Attach the working parts
buildSteps.detail: Sensing strands, motor legs and payloads are added by DNA hybridisation or covalent linkers at defined positions.

buildSteps.title: Package it
buildSteps.detail: The robot is wrapped in a lipid vesicle or polymer coat so it survives enzymes and immune cells in the bloodstream.

buildSteps.title: Test on cells
buildSteps.detail: Single-molecule fluorescence and microfluidics show whether the gates fire and the walker actually steps along its track — kinesin advances 8 nm per molecule of ATP.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Dosing, organ distribution, immune reaction and clearance are measured; this is where most designs fail.

buildSteps.title: Scale up manufacture
buildSteps.detail: Consistent, sterile, batch-to-batch-identical production of a nanostructure with hundreds of parts is an unsolved engineering problem.

prerequisites.why: proved in 2006 and now routine in laboratories for shapes up to a few hundred nanometres.
logic gates work reliably in a test tube but behave unpredictably inside cells and serum.
kinesin and synthetic DNA walkers move along engineered tracks in vitro, not through living tissue.
liver uptake is solved; reaching most other tissues and tumours selectively is not.

prerequisites.tech: Real-time control and imaging at nanometre scale
prerequisites.why: there is no way to see or steer an individual robot inside a living person, so it must act autonomously.
nucleic acid structures are degraded by nucleases and cleared by the liver within hours to days.

pathway.milestone: DNA robots that sort cargo on a surface, and a nanorobot that shrank tumours in mice (2018) by exposing a clotting enzyme only at tumour vessels
pathway.unlocks: proof that molecular logic and targeting can change an outcome in a living animal.

pathway.milestone: multifunctional structures with several logic gates and a payload, validated in animal models
pathway.unlocks: selectivity high enough to justify human safety trials.

pathway.milestone: molecular machines switched from outside the body by ultrasound, magnetic fields or light, acting on cell surfaces
pathway.unlocks: a way to control the device without imaging it directly.

pathway.milestone: reliable delivery to solid organs and tumour interiors, not just the liver
autonomous repair inside a single cell
pathway.unlocks: medicine at the molecular scale — but it requires onboard power, navigation and a defence against immune clearance that do not yet exist.
